title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, the mother's body needs to be provided with adequate nutrients to support the development of the fetus. One of the most important nutrients during this period is folic acid. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus.

## Folic Acid and Iron in First Trimester Nutrition

Folic acid is a crucial nutrient during the early stages of pregnancy. It helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus, including spina bifida and anencephaly. To ensure adequate folic acid intake, pregnant women should consume foods rich in folic acid such as leafy greens, fruits, and dairy products.

Iron is also an essential nutrient during this period. Iron helps support the development of the fetus and prevents anemia in the mother. Iron-rich foods include red meat, chicken, fish, and legumes.

## Safer Foods During the First Trimester

During the first trimester, pregnant women need to be cautious when choosing foods to ensure safety for both the mother and the fetus. The following foods should be avoided:

* Raw or undercooked foods: Foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw meat can contain harmful bacteria that can affect the fetus.
* Foods containing listeria: Listeria is a type of bacteria that can harm the fetus. Foods that contain listeria include soft cheeses, unpasteurized milk, and cold cuts.
* Foods containing mercury: Mercury is a toxic substance that can harm the fetus. Foods that contain mercury include shark, swordfish, and king mackerel.

## Cooking Foods Safely

To ensure safety for both the mother and the fetus, pregnant women need to cook foods thoroughly before consumption. The following are some safe cooking methods:

* Cooking meat: Meat should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure safety.
* Cooking fish: Fish should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to ensure safety.
* Cooking eggs: Eggs should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure safety.

## Conclusion

First trimester nutrition is crucial to support the development of the fetus. Pregnant women need to provide adequate nutrients, including folic acid and iron, and avoid unsafe foods.
